clue.text: In the morning, applies language to a ridiculous degree

indicators.note: the words for the morning are wrapped around the next pieces, so they sit in it

parts.note: AM is the usual abbreviation for the morning (ante meridiem)
to apply paint or ointment lightly is to dab it on
Urdu is a language of Pakistan and India

explanation.surface: Someone smears on a foreign tongue each morning to an absurd extent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used for an argument pushed to an absurd extreme.

annotationWithheld.why: Upset grandee (7): 'Upset' is both the definition and the only anagram indicator for GRANDEE (the blog notes it doubles up)

clue.text: Head of Scottish party

parts.note: bean is informal slang for the head
in Scots speech 'of' is shortened to o'

explanation.surface: A clan chief is introduced as the leader of a Scottish political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' and 'party' look like a party leader; the head is BEAN and 'party' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British slang for a lively celebration or spree.

clue.text: "Word" and "Lord" are in performance of rude hymn

indicators.note: a performance reworks the rude hymn's letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A coarse song pairs two words at the end of its lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words look as if they rhyme but are said differently, so they are only an eye rhyme: the pair do not actually rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that look alike on the page but differ in sound are not truly rhymed.

clue.text: 3's lively dance includes Olympian idea

indicators.note: the rearranged dance letters hold the next pieces within them
a lively version stirs the letters of dance into a new order

parts.note: Jessica Ennis won heptathlon gold at the 2012 Olympics
a theme is a central idea

explanation.surface: A comic's energetic dance number carries an Olympic motif.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to the answer at 3 down, the British children's comic, and the definition is one of its characters; 'idea' looks like a thought, but is the unifying motif.
explanation.definitionFit: This mischievous boy with his dog Gnasher is a long-running character in the comic.

clue.text: 3's car sounds definitely an old one

indicators.note: the small car's name is said aloud to give a girl's name

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car
the is the definite article
the Hillman Minx was a British family car of the mid twentieth century

explanation.surface: A comic strip's motoring section describes the noise of a vintage vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' is the comic at 3 down; the definition is one of its characters. The Hillman Minx was a British saloon car made from the 1930s to 1970.
explanation.definitionFit: This naughty girl in a striped jumper is a long-running strip character in the comic.

clue.text: City where one may pull the plug on a singer

definitions.meaning: a Roman spa city in Somerset, England

definitions.text: where one may pull the plug on a singer
definitions.meaning: people sing in the tub, then pull out the plug to drain it

explanation.surface: A city where a vocalist might be silenced abruptly.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the English spa city; the other is a tub where people famously sing.

clue.text: Retired accountant taps into unimaginative orgy

indicators.note: the reversed accountant and the taps are put inside the dull word

parts.note: banal means trite and unimaginative

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
C and H mark the cold and hot taps

explanation.surface: A dull bookkeeper in retirement joins a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taps' looks like a verb meaning draws on; it is the pair of tap labels, C and H. 'Retired' turns CA into AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacchanal is a drunken revel, named after the rites of Bacchus.

clue.text: See 6
Refrain from calamari appetiser

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: Avoid eating the squid starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain from' reads as 'avoid'; 'Refrain' is the definition (a song) and 'from' signals the letters lifted out of the words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrain is a song or tune, and an aria is a solo song in opera.

clue.text: Before newspaperman reported dispatch of chicken and pheasant, maybe

indicators.note: the spoken phrase comes first, ahead of the editor
the phrase is spoken, so a word sounding the same is written

parts.note: killing a chicken is done by wringing its neck
ED is the editor of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Before a journalist's report, a chicken was killed along with a pheasant.
explanation.walkthrough: WRING NECK said aloud sounds the same as RING NECK.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheasant species with a white collar is called ring-necked, so this describes such a bird.

clue.text: See 26
Murdoch starts joining in short drunken dance

parts.note: Iris Murdoch was a British novelist

indicators.note: the initial is placed inside the shortened word
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: high can mean intoxicated

indicators.note: the starts of the word joining give its opening letter

explanation.surface: A novelist joins in an inebriated dance.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH loses its final H to give HIG, with J inside after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A jig is a lively folk dance, and this one is associated with Ireland.

clue.text: Any centre could be used for celebration

explanation.definitionFit: A hundredth anniversary is commonly marked with a celebration.

clue.text: Close result of one x two — three

indicators.note: the letters emerge as a product from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Multiplying one by two gives an answer near three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three' with its dash nods to counting: after one and two comes three, so the answer is what follows in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means nearest or adjacent, as in the house close by.

clue.text: Had more girl-friends than was fashionable

definitions.text: Had more girl-friends than was fashionable

parts.words: Had more girl-friends than was fashionable
parts.note: read as 'had more dates than' it describes a ladies' man; read whole it means no longer in vogue

explanation.surface: A man has had more girlfriends than was the done thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dated or old-fashioned has gone out of style.

clue.text: Amaze with short trick

indicators.note: short means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a stunt is a trick or feat

explanation.surface: Astonish people with a quick conjuring trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish or stagger someone.

clue.text: Crush tree tops with weight

indicators.note: only the top letters of tree are kept, losing its tail

parts.note: an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Flatten the top branches with a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops' keeps the top two letters of 'tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to beat or crush an opponent decisively.

clue.text: Even quail cooked in 112.5?

indicators.note: the cooked bird letters sit inside the compass point

parts.note: 112.5 degrees on a compass is east-south-east

indicators.note: cooking reworks the letters of quail

explanation.surface: A bird prepared at exactly the right temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 112.5 is a bearing in degrees, not a temperature: east-south-east, ESE.
explanation.definitionFit: To even something is to make it level or equal.

clue.text: Admit president's vice limited damage

indicators.note: the sin hems in the damage, enclosing it

parts.note: a vice is a sin
wear is damage from use, as in wear and tear

explanation.surface: A president's bad habit kept the harm in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stops at 'president'; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To induct a president into office, an oath of office is administered to them.

clue.text: Viciously set about free march

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the next piece
vicious treatment jumbles the letters of set

parts.note: to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A violent mob surrounds a protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viciously' looks like an adverb describing the marchers; it only signals that the letters of 'set' are rearranged, and 'about' wraps them around the free piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long step in walking, as in a march.

clue.text: Confirmed he'd got red revolutionary in 3

indicators.note: a revolutionary overturns the order of he'd got red

explanation.surface: A man said he had been converted to communism in the comic.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' is the comic at 3 down; the answer is one of its characters.
explanation.definitionFit: This trickster boy who dodges trouble is a strip character in the comic.

clue.text: See 22
Potter production sad elf took part in

clue.text: Aint bathin' bad for the liver?

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Not bathing is harmful to a vital organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liver' looks like the organ; it is one who lives somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant is a person who lives or dwells in a place.

clue.text: 3's ground also turned into city

parts.note: Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: turned means read backwards

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: A comic's ground was also converted into a city.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' is the comic at 3 down, and the answer is its top-hatted aristocrat; Lord's is a London cricket ground, and 'turned' reads 'also' backwards before 'into' puts it inside the city.

clue.text: Extremely light

clue.text: Changing drug activity in gay club

in a gay club the activity is men dating
